dossier.architecture: Turreted swerve scorer with compliant collector and rotating climber.

subsystems.drivetrain: SDS MK4; L3 gearing changed to L1 after Texas State for acceleration under load.
subsystems.intake: Foam-tile dead-axle roller, sacrificial polycarbonate shield and tubing compliance; two pneumatic positions protect the deployment cylinder.
subsystems.transfer: Four omni rollers feed a kicker that isolates cargo from the spinning flywheel.
subsystems.scoring: Two-Falcon main wheel, powered upper roller, turret and rack-adjusted hood. Coarser rack addressed tooth skipping.
subsystems.endgame: Three-motor rotating mechanism with deploy motor, locking clips and center-of-gravity shift; interview reports roughly 5–6-second climbs.
subsystems.controls: Turret/range control decouples collection heading from scoring aim.

versions: Hood rack revised; rotating climb swing transfer improved. IRI interview is postseason.
dossier.analysis: Collector compliance and acceleration are throughput mechanisms. Turret sophistication is valuable only when the intake, isolation kicker and chassis consistently supply clean shots.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-118 · Acceleration, protected acquisition and climb CG were iterated separately
context_documents.body:
# 2022-118: Acceleration, protected acquisition and climb CG were iterated separately

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The retained technical account describes a compliant dead-axis intake, isolated kicker, turret and adjustable hood. A coarser hood rack addressed skipping. The interview describes changing drivetrain gearing for acceleration under defense and shifting climb CG by rotating the arm.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly reports insufficient acceleration after States and a one-to-two-second climb improvement from the CG change.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Maximum free speed is not defended cycle performance. Climb timing also depends on gravitational motion and hook approach, not merely winch speed. Separate the filmed later configuration from earlier competitions.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure loaded acceleration, hood backlash and repeatable climb completion, preserving the reported timing conditions.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Robonauts team interview at Indiana Robotics Invitational
source_reviews.locator: 1:24–2:47 drive; 2:47–6:06 intake; 6:06–9:16 feeder and shooter; 9:28–11:58 climb
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
source_reviews.facts: Team explains the fast gear change, serviceable impact parts, separate powered launch surfaces and center-of-gravity shift during climb.
source_reviews.limitations: Later offseason interview. Ratios stated from memory are treated as approximate.

source_reviews.title: Horizon post-interview technical discussion
source_reviews.review_basis: Read full replies in saved Discourse JSON
source_reviews.facts: Explains intake packaging and durability, gearing changes, low-voltage shot issue and climb design.
source_reviews.limitations: Several dimensions and ratios are recalled rather than verified against CAD.

source_reviews.title: Official Horizon code archive
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team C++ implementation inside release ZIP
source_reviews.facts: Debounced cargo counting and separate kick states. Climb operator interface exposes deploy, claws and closed-loop setpoints.
source_reviews.limitations: Read 2022 directory separately from later work in the archive.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Horizon’s fast swerve cycles, turret and adjustable launcher were paired with a narrow rotary traversal climber. The intake’s size came from putting a large roller on an arm that could clear the shooter in its initial stowed position. The narrow upper package left room for partners on the traversal rung, while the wide lower intake was designed for contact during cargo cycles.
source_review.piece_flow: Large compliant foam wheels gather and center cargo. Guides and an interior omni-wheel feeder carry it toward the turret. A separate kicker holds cargo away from the spinning launcher until commanded, then pushes it into the main flywheel and independently driven upper wheel. The released kicker code counts two debounced beam inputs and supports firing, reversing and idle drive.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The long intake arms stow over the shooter and deploy through a large sweep. A replaceable polycarbonate strike surface, fence rollers, surgical tubing and landing saddles handle different contact loads. The narrow turret and climber package depends on coordinating the hood and yaw before the climber rotates. The team reports using less than 14 inches of traversal rung.

subsystems.name: Swerve drive
subsystems.construction: SDS Mk4 modules with preconfigured replacement assemblies.
subsystems.operation: The team started with L3, tried L1 and L2 after district championship and chose L1.
subsystems.team_rationale: Improve acceleration under defense on a full-weight robot. Mk4s were lighter and simpler to replace for the team.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compare acceleration, braking and recovery after contact over the actual cycle. Do not choose ratio on unloaded top speed alone.
subsystems.interfaces: Module plates, bumper, connectors and drivetrain tuning.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Team observed plates bending upward. Inspect mount flatness and confirm spare module offsets after swaps.

subsystems.name: Collector and feed
subsystems.construction: Large foam contact wheels on a dead-axle assembly, long box-tube arms and staged pneumatic deployment.
subsystems.operation: Guide cargo over the entrance to a powered omni feeder and then into a separately controlled kicker.
subsystems.team_rationale: Capture quickly, withstand wall contact and swap damaged surfaces or complete rollers.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Arm length amplifies impact moment. A replaceable contact surface limits service cost only if the remaining load bypasses weak bearings and actuator rods.
subsystems.interfaces: Pivot clearance, bumper, kicker, foam roller wear and climb envelope.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check distorted arms, loose belts and pieces held at the feeder junction.
subsystems.unknowns: Capture data by approach speed and wear state.

subsystems.name: Launcher and turret
subsystems.construction: Two-Falcon main wheel, independently driven upper wheel, geared hood and hollow turret gear.
subsystems.operation: Feeder delivers through the yaw axis. Fast turret and hood motion set aim and trajectory.
subsystems.team_rationale: Keep up with turning chassis and manage ball spin.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Size the upper wheel for torque and speed margin at low voltage. A faster idle mechanism is irrelevant if it cannot reach its commanded speed during a shot.
subsystems.interfaces: Power bus, range estimate, shot table and feeder.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Look for hood gear skipping and top-wheel saturation during current peaks.
subsystems.unknowns: Shot dispersion and published configuration per event.

subsystems.name: Rotary traversal
subsystems.construction: Motorized deployment, mechanical latches and three-Falcon chain-driven rotation.
subsystems.operation: Prepare hood and turret, capture successive rungs and use a small rotation to shift CG for the last transfer.
subsystems.team_rationale: Use narrow rung width, improve smoothness and finish quickly.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Separate deployment from load-bearing rotation. Assess changing torque and swing about each rung, plus voltage under concurrent loads.
subsystems.interfaces: Claw commands, rung geometry, shooter stow and partner envelopes.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Verify both supports before transfer and recovery from missed capture.
subsystems.unknowns: Loaded timing distribution and full match configuration.

revisions: L3 to L1 after defense testing. Electric climb deployment replaced the earlier pneumatic actuator. A larger motor and revised upper-wheel gearing addressed low-voltage saturation before Championship. Team also describes changing hood rack tooth size after skipping.
transferable_principles: Plan service access and spares at major impact interfaces. Validate cycle-critical actuators at match voltage with realistic concurrent demand.
disconfirming_conditions: Longer protected sprints may change the gearing result. Different bar spacing, CG or partner envelopes can defeat the same rotary transfer. A fixed-azimuth electric-only adaptation needs revised packaging and deployment.
remaining_gaps: Older dossier used for navigation. No CAD measurement, independent timing, or complete mapping of released XML configurations to events.
recommended_images: Team robots page https://www.118robonauts.org/robots, Horizon in 118 workspace with banners photo. Pair with a loaded transfer image showing the narrow rung occupancy.
